key_insight: Three-dimensional DSMC captures measured jet-induced interference pressure in rarefied hypersonic crossflow, while two-dimensional models reproduce its structure but overpredict peak magnitude about twelvefold.
engineering_relevance: Accurate reaction-control-jet interference predictions in rarefied hypersonic flight require resolving three-dimensional kinetic effects.
method: Revisit a 1975 DLR helium-jet experiment in Mach 11–12 air crossflow at three freestream densities.
Compare 2D and 3D DSMC simulations over Knudsen numbers 0.021–0.125.
Check planar-model resolution convergence and plate-alone boundary-layer consistency.
evidence_signal: At all three densities, 3D DSMC matches measured interference-pressure lobe peaks within 25% and their positions within 3 mm; the most rarefied 2D case converges within 1% of its extrapolated limit.
watch_item: Both models overpredict plate-alone wall pressure by 50–75%, and lateral relief remains an unconfirmed explanation for the 2D discrepancy.
paper_title: Kinetic study of Reaction-Control-Jet Interference in Rarefied Hypersonic Crossflow
